prize_parts.citation: For conceiving and demonstrating targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional small molecules that recruit E3 ubiquitin ligases to chosen proteins
For the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: I have moved my configuration. In round 1 I paired sequencing-by-synthesis with base editing as reading and rewriting DNA, but the exchange shows that B001 is held only by me, while B061 has four explicit supporters naming Liu alone and B007 has three supporters who agree that Crews and Deshaies conceived and first demonstrated heterobifunctional degraders. The pair B007 with B061 is the only configuration already put forward by a member other than me that combines the two most supported ballots, and it has a real common principle: a chemist designs a small, defined molecular event that redirects a natural biological machine, ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis for proteins, deaminase chemistry for DNA bases, with the 'previously unforeseen opportunities' I care about as a physicist looking for new capability. Both rest on well-understood mechanisms (ternary-complex cooperativity, directed evolution of a deaminase), both are independently reproduced, and the two attributions can be stated in three names: Crews and Deshaies for the concept and first demonstration, Liu for both editor families. Stopping the degrader part at the concept keeps the original discovery separate from later refinement, which is the distinction I ask every member to make.
statement.case_against: The two parts are different areas and the link is thematic, so a critic may say the pairing exists to bridge first choices. B007 has no approved degrader yet, and a citation that stops at Crews and Deshaies leaves out Ciulli, whose VHL ligands made the approach drug-like, and Handa, whose identification of cereblon explained thalidomide, and it ignores Sakamoto's co-authored first proof of principle. B061 follows the 2020 CRISPR prize, long-term safety is unsettled, and the Nishida and Kondo concurrent cytidine-deaminase work is not fully resolved by a Liu-alone attribution. Dropping sequencing means giving up the more mature and widely deployed field, and I accept that cost.

responses.point: Brzezinski proposes Crews and Deshaies for B007 and Liu for B061, one achievement acting on proteins and one on nucleic acids, and explicitly accepts that Ciulli and Handa must be left out to fit three names.
responses.response: I now arrive at your configuration and want to say why I accept your trade-off. The three-name cap forces a cut somewhere, and the only cut that separates the original discovery from refinements is the concept and first demonstration of heterobifunctional degraders; Ciulli's ligand work and the cereblon glue strand are important but build on it. I share your worry that preference for mechanism should not decide by default, so I add one condition: the B007 citation must say heterobifunctional degraders explicitly and not claim the glue mechanism, so it is defensible against Handa and Ito.

responses.point: Chabes places B007 first and adds Handa so that the cereblon glue mechanism and PROTACs are one principle, writing both into the citation.
responses.response: I take your point that B007 is the strongest conceptual case and I have moved it into my preferred configuration. I do not follow you on Handa, because the cereblon discovery is a distinct mechanistic breakthrough about how existing drugs act, not a design principle, and Aili is right that writing it into one citation blurs what was discovered. With a cap of three people and Liu occupying one seat, I cannot name Handa without dropping Deshaies. I also concede your earlier argument on 1980: that was a different invention, but it does not rescue sequencing for me now that no one else backs it.

responses.point: Aili supports Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli under a PROTAC-centred citation, but notes the objection that approval-level clinical proof is pending and that cereblon and Sakamoto create attribution risk.
responses.response: Your three-person story is coherent, and Ciulli's structural and thermodynamic work on ternary complexes did turn the concept into a design discipline. In a single-part B007 prize I would be open to it. In a two-part prize with Liu, giving B007 three names breaches the three-person ceiling, so I prefer the concept pair and I would want to hear whether you can accept B061 alongside B007 on those terms, since you list B061 as your first alternative.

responses.point: Aqvist makes B061 his whole prize, with Liu alone, a clean attribution distinct from the 2020 CRISPR nuclease prize, and lists B007 as a second alternative.
responses.response: I agree with your account of the chemistry and of why base editing is distinct from the 2020 prize. On Nishida and Kondo, the editors came from concurrent work, but the adenine base editor needed a deaminase evolved for a substrate no natural enzyme accepts and the conception and engineering of both families trace to Liu, so I keep Liu alone while saying openly that this is the weakest point of the part. I would ask you whether a B007 second part is acceptable to you, since that is the practical difference between your single-part prize and mine.

uncertainties: Whether the absence of an approved degrader makes B007 too early, and whether I should weigh that more heavily than the committee's majority does.
Whether Nishida and Kondo's concurrent cytidine-deaminase work is close enough in time and substance that a Liu-alone attribution would be criticised.
Whether the two-part pairing has a convincing common principle or only bridges differing first choices.
Whether the 2020 CRISPR prize makes B061 a second genome-editing prize in the eyes of the wider community.
statement.conflict_note: No change: I have no personal tie to any shortlisted candidate or credited person. My research interest in single-molecule nanoscale devices is closest to the nanopore ballot B044, which is no longer in my alternatives and which I would weigh on its merits only. I share a Lund affiliation with Somfai and Sparr, which carries no stake in any candidate.
